blocks.text: I do not set out a priori to create a specific type of photograph. On the contrary, I take a photo when something catches my eye—a color, a shape, a situation, or an atmosphere—and over time families of images emerge naturally around a few recurring themes such as those featured on my website: “transparency”, “urban traces”, “surfaces” and “geometry.” Photos with a unique identity – those in the “sui generis” theme – do not belong to any specific family, yet they may well contain the seed of a future theme.

The images in this portfolio belong to the “transparency” theme. I have always been drawn to scenes where the interplay of light and the translucency of materials render the subject ambiguous, opening it up to various interpretations.

Some photographers and artists who have most inspired and/or helped me in my work: my father Gunther Gerzso, Ralph Gibson, Philippe Gontier, Alain Fleischer, Ansel Adams, Harry Gruyaert, Manuel Alvarez Bravo, David Hockney, Paul Klee, Edward Hopper, Raphael, Caravaggio.
